expectations.text: Identifies this as an exhauster over a KNOWN, enumerable queue and enumerates the call sites up front
expectations.evidence: "Archetype: Exhauster. The work is a *known, enumerable* list — every `logInfo(` call site is discoverable with a grep up front and the set only shrinks." plus §3.1 "Enumerate deterministically. `rg -n 'logInfo\s*\('` ... Emit `queue.json` ... pin `total` from this count in code"

expectations.text: Defines a per-item done-criterion verified by a SEPARATE agent (compiles / type-checks / tests pass), not the worker's own say-so
expectations.evidence: "A file is `verified` only when a verifier that is a *different agent than the worker*..." with clauses "Compiles | `tsc --noEmit` ... exits 0", "Tests pass", and "A worker never certifies its own file."

expectations.text: Fails closed: an unverified or failed site returns to the queue and becomes a NAMED blocked item after bounded retries, never a silent skip
expectations.evidence: "it returns to the queue under `MAX_RETRIES`, and it **stays in the denominator**"; "A file with an unmappable call, or one whose tests keep failing after `MAX_RETRIES`, becomes a *named* blocked item."

expectations.text: Counts progress deterministically (done/total) and reports terminal 'blocked' if any site is unverified rather than a percentage-done success
expectations.evidence: "Progress = `confirmed_files / total_files`, computed in the driver from verified verdicts." and "`199/200` verified with one blocked reports **`blocked`**, not `99.5%`."

expectations.text: Includes a budget ceiling / model tiering and an observable ledger of item states, not just a for-loop that trusts each edit
expectations.evidence: "Budget ceiling + tiering. Hard token cap with a reserve so finalize runs; cheap model for enumerate/ledger, mid for worker/verify, strong only for stuck/blocked files." plus §7 "Every round writes `progress.json`: `files done / total`, the in-flight batch ... the **blocked list**."
